supporting_observations.claim: The reported PowerShell activity is recorded at 13:42:01 UTC, rather than exactly 13:40 UTC. It ran as NWD\sam.okafor and invoked the organization's stated workstation patch script, \\FILE-NWD-01\Admin\Apply-Updates.ps1.
Shortly before the process started, WS-ICHEN-01 recorded a network logon for sam.okafor from WS-SOKAFOR-01; the PowerShell process has the same logon ID.
The script's observed activity is consistent with patching: PowerShell connected through the proxy to download.windowsupdate.com, and then launched wusa to install a Windows update package quietly.
The PowerShell process exited about 46 seconds after it started; the observed wusa process also exited shortly after launch.

The observed account, source workstation, script path, and update activity align with the supplied IT patching practice and scheduled business-hours workstation patching. The available evidence supports a benign disposition for the alerted activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records show the PowerShell command line, but do not include the contents or hash of Apply-Updates.ps1 or the downloaded update package.
The ticket reports a window appearing around 13:40 UTC, while the recorded PowerShell start is 13:42:01 UTC; the evidence does not establish the exact time the user saw a window.
The records establish process execution and network activity, but do not independently confirm the change-calendar entry or patch completion.
claims_not_established: Whether the user saw the PowerShell window at precisely 13:40 UTC.
Whether the script or update package contents were modified or tampered with; their contents and hashes are not provided.
unrelated_findings: Webex.exe was launched with an app.slack.com URL; this is outside the alerted PowerShell activity and may warrant separate review against software and service policy. (T044-00168, T044-00170)

DC-NWD-01 made connection attempts to WS-ICHEN-01 on ports 8080, 443, and 445 that were rejected, and a connection attempt to port 135 did not complete; these are separate from the alerted patching activity. (T044-00127, T044-00128, T044-00130, T044-00131, T044-00132, T044-00133, T044-00134)
